([[Chief Executive Officer]]) | website = {{url|burton.co.uk}} }} '''Burton Online Limited''' (trading as '''Burton Menswear''') is a British online clothing retailer, former [[high street]] retailer and clothing manufacturer, specialising in men's clothing and footwear. It is operated by [[Debenhams Group]] in the [[United Kingdom]]. Previously, Burton was a constituent of the [[FTSE 100 Index]], but became a trading name of ''Arcadia Group Brands Ltd'', part of the [[Arcadia Group]]. [[Sir Philip Green]] acquired the Arcadia Group in 2002, and it became the sole owner of Burton. In 2021, [[Boohoo.com|Boohoo Group]] (now Debenhams Group) acquired the brand after Arcadia went into [[Administration in United Kingdom law|administration]]. ==History== [[File:BurtonsLS9.jpg|thumb|right|The Burtons factory in [[Burmantofts]], [[Leeds]], is now used only as a warehouse]] The company was founded by [[Sir Montague Maurice Burton]] in [[Chesterfield, Derbyshire|Chesterfield]] in 1903 under the name of The Cross-Tailoring Company.{{cite web |url=http://www.burton.co.uk/en/bruk/category/company-info-5464143/home |title=About Us |year=2013 |website=Burton Menswear London |access-date=14 February 2018 |archive-date=1 February 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180201224721/http://www.burton.co.uk/en/bruk/category/company-info-5464143/home |url-status=dead }} It was first listed on the [[London Stock Exchange]] in 1929 by which time it had 400 stores, factories and mills. After [[World War II]], Montague Burton was one of the suppliers of [[demob suit]]s to the British government for [[Demobilisation of the British Armed Forces after the Second World War|demobilising]] servicemen, comprising jacket, trousers, waistcoat, shirt and underwear. It has been speculated that this is the origin of the phrase "[[The Full Monty (phrase)|the full monty]]". In 1946, the company acquired the [[Peter Robinson (department store)|Peter Robinson]] department store chain.{{Cite web|url=http://www.arcadiagroup.co.uk/about/group_history.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081209020056/http://www.arcadiagroup.co.uk/about/group_history.html|url-status=dead|title=Arcadia History|archive-date=9 December 2008}} Montague Burton died in 1952. By this time, the company was the largest multiple tailor in the world.{{Citation needed|date=December 2020}} The company expanded by purchasing various other brands, including competitors until it was split from [[Debenhams]] in 1998.{{Clarify|reason=Does the preceding sentence mean that Burton ceased purchasing other brands when Debenhams demerged from it?|date=March 2021}} At this time Burtons became a brand name, and the [[Arcadia Group]] name took over as the group name.{{Citation needed|date=December 2020}} The companies purchased or merged with were: *1954{{Snd}}Jackson the Tailor{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=kRYNAQAAIAAJ&pg=PA152|title=Montague Burton: The Tailor of Taste By Eric M. Sigsworth|access-date=10 November 2015|page=152|isbn=9780719023644 |last1=Sigsworth |first1=Eric M. |year=1990 |publisher=Manchester University Press }} *1979{{Snd}}[[Dorothy Perkins]] *1984{{Snd}}[[Harry Fenton (designer)|Harry Fenton]]{{cite web|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=2507&dat=19840327&id=AsFAAAAAIBAJ&sjid=2qUMAAAAIBAJ&pg=3867,6154997&hl=en|title=Combined English looks to be out of the wood - The Glasgow Herald p.27 March 1984|access-date=4 December 2015}} *1985{{Snd}}Debenhams *1986{{Snd}}[[John Collier (clothing retailer)|John Collier]] Burton was the official clothing supplier to the [[England national football team]] for the [[1966 FIFA World Cup]], [[UEFA Euro 1996]] and the [[2002 FIFA World Cup]] championships. In 1998 the company changed its name to [[Arcadia Group]].{{cite news |title=Arcadia's clearance sale |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/business/1260313.stm |newspaper=BBC News |date=4 April 2001 |access-date=23 September 2013}} Philip Green purchased the company in 2002. The Burton company archives are held at the West Yorkshire Archive Service in Leeds.[http://www.archives.wyjs.org.uk West Yorkshire Archive Service, Leeds] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090501062045/http://www.archives.wyjs.org.uk/ |date=1 May 2009 }} In July 2020, Arcadia Group, which comprised several brands including Burton, had been hit hard by the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom|COVID-19 lockdown]] and planned hundreds of job cuts to minimise costs.{{Cite web|date=1 July 2020|title=jobs as latest Covid-19 victim|url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/money/breaking-philip-greens-fashion-group-22283391|access-date=7 July 2020|website=Mirror}} As financial difficulties worsened, Arcadia entered [[Administration in United Kingdom law|administration]] on 30 November 2020.{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-55139369|title=Topshop owner Arcadia goes into administration|work=BBC News|date=30 November 2020|access-date=30 November 2020}} In February 2021, Boohoo.com announced it was buying the Burton brand from Arcadia (along with the Wallis and Dorothy Perkins brands) for £25.2 million, with the loss of around 2,450 jobs.{{Cite news|date=2021-02-08|title=Boohoo buys Dorothy Perkins, Wallis and Burton but 2,450 jobs lost|language=en-GB|work=BBC News|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/business-55977587|access-date=2021-02-08}} All Burton stores closed as the company became an online only retailer.{{Cite web |last=Robinson |first=Jon |date=2022-12-09 |title=Debenhams reports losses as Boohoo's brands suffer mixed fortunes |url=https://www.business-live.co.uk/retail-consumer/debenhams-losses-revealed-boohoo-group-25710983 |access-date=2023-08-30 |website=Business Live |language=en}} ==Architecture== [[File:Art_Deco_Burton_Abergavenny.jpg|thumb|right|Art Deco Burton store in [[Burton, Abergavenny|Abergavenny]]]] Beginning in 1923, Burton began to acquire freehold sites in order to build its own custom designed stores.{{cite web |url=http://www.britishlistedbuildings.co.uk/wa-83477-burton-s-building-aberystwyth#.VqYhzfmLS70 |title=Burton's Building, Aberystwyth |website=britishlistedbuildings.co.uk |access-date=27 January 2016}} Prominent town centre corner sites were preferred and the shops often moved a few doors along the same street in order to acquire the corner site. Leeds-based architect Harry Wilson was hired at this time and developed the Burton "house style" building design. In 1931 Burton took over Wilson's practice to make it the in-house architecture department.{{cite book | last = Skinner | first = Joan S. | title = Form and Fancy: Factories and Factory Buildings by Wallis, Gilbert & Partners, 1916-1939 | url = https://archive.org/details/formfancyfactori0000skin | url-access = registration | publisher = [[Liverpool University Press]] | edition = 1st | location = Liverpool | date = 1997 | page = [https://archive.org/details/formfancyfactori0000skin/page/215 215] | isbn = 0853236127}} Wilson was replaced as chief architect by Nathaniel Martin in 1937. This Burton in-house architecture was [[Art Deco]] in style. Individual stores vary from the more restrained red-brick with neoclassical scroll headed columns to fully-fledged Art Deco with glazed white [[glazed architectural terra-cotta|faience]] tile, geometric patterns and stylised elephant heads. However, there are also many standard elements such as a wide polished black granite band above the shop windows for signage, metal vent grates bearing the company logo, billiard halls on the upper levels, window lights showing the locations of other Burton stores, and mosaic titles{{Snd}}sometimes including the company logo{{Snd}}in the doorways. [[File:Montague Burton Building, Dublin, Ireland.jpg|thumb|The [[Montague Burton Building]] in [[Dublin]] is on the city's list of protected structures. ]] At ground level, foundation stones were often placed by Montague Burton's four children, Barbara, Stanley, Arnold and Raymond. Each store might have one or several foundation stones, each bearing one name and the year. For example: "This stone laid by Raymond Montaque Burton 1937". The children were quite young when these stones were laid. Stanley Howard was born in 1914{{cite web|url=http://www.movinghere.org.uk/galleries/histories/jewish/working_lives/montague_burton5.htm |archive-url=http://webarchive.nationalarchives.gov.uk/20131105222903/http://www.movinghere.org.uk/galleries/histories/jewish/working_lives/montague_burton5.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=5 November 2013 |title=Sir Montague Burton and his Business Expansion |website=Moving Here Migration Histories |access-date=16 November 2016 |first=Brett |last=Harrison}} and laid a stone for the [[Nottingham]] [[Beastmarket Hill]] store in 1924. At least six stores bear stones laid by Montague's wife "Lady Burton", and a number in the mid to late 1930s were laid by Austin Stephen Burton who may have been a grandchild.{{cite web |url=http://www.londonremembers.com/subjects/austin-stephen-burton?memorial_id=3952 |title=Austin Stephen Burton |website=londonremembers.com |access-date=28 January 2016}} Whilst some of these Burton buildings have been destroyed over the years, many are still standing and some of them still have active snooker clubs upstairs. Some were still occupied by Burton stores at the time of Arcadia's closure in 2020 (often a combined Burton and [[Dorothy Perkins]] store) but many others had changed use. McDonald's first three restaurants in the UK were opened in former Burton stores in 1974 and 1975 as the company was selling property at that time.{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/foodanddrink/11228085/McDonalds-amazing-growth-in-UK.html |title=McDonald's amazing growth in UK |first=Harry |last=Wallop |date=13 November 2014 |newspaper=The Telegraph |access-date=28 January 2016}} Most of the Scottish stores are listed with [[Historic Environment Scotland]], protecting them from changes.{{efn|Listed Scottish stores include Aberdeen,{{cite web |url=https://britishlistedbuildings.co.uk/200355839-21a-st-nicholas-street-aberdeen-aberdeen |title=21A St Nicholas Street, Aberdeen}}{{cite web |url=https://britishlistedbuildings.co.uk/200399608-topshop-topman-73-77-odd-nos-union-street-aberdeen |title=Topshop Topman, 73-77 (Odd Nos) Union Street}} Aberystwyth, Kirkcaldy,{{cite web |url=https://britishlistedbuildings.co.uk/200390707-burtons-89-95-high-street-kirkcaldy-kirkcaldy |title=Burton's, 89-95 High Street, Kirkcaldy |website=britishlistedbuildings.co.uk}} Paisley{{cite web |url=https://britishlistedbuildings.co.uk/200398079-burtons-6-and-8-high-street-paisley |title=Burton's, 6 And 8 High Street}}}} However, only six stores in [[England]] and [[Wales]] are [[listed buildings]],{{efn|Listed stores in England and Wales include Abergavenny{{cite web |url=https://britishlistedbuildings.co.uk/300014875-burton-abergavenny |title=Burton}} and Camden.{{cite web |url=https://britishlistedbuildings.co.uk/101379031-burtons-headquarters-and-shop-bloomsbury-ward |title=Burtons Headquarters and Shop}}}} leaving over 200 with no protection from future changes or demolition. {{As of|2021}}, stores have been demolished in [[Plymouth]] (2004){{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/devon/news_features/2004/drakes_circus_work.shtml |title=City centre revamp is under way |website=bbc.co.uk |access-date=28 January 2016}} and [[Neasden]] (2012).{{cite web |url=http://whatpub.com/pubs/NLD/6223/galway-hooker-willesden |title=Galway Hooker |website=whatpub.com |access-date=28 January 2016}}{{Update inline|date=March 2021|?=yes|reason=It is possible that stores have been demolished more recently. Previous wording of the preceding sentence did not specify 'as of'; 'as of 2021' was added later and may be incorrect.}} An early [[Dublin]] Burton's store was housed in the purpose-built [[Montague Burton Building]] on the corner of [[Dame Street]] and [[South Great George's Street]]. It is now on the city's list of protected structures.{{Cite web |date=2018-09-05 |title=Record of Protected Structures |url=https://www.dublincity.ie/residential/planning/archaeology-conservation-heritage/record-protected-structures |access-date=2022-07-13 |website=Dublin City Council |language=en}} ==Charitable activities== [[File:Burtons, East Ham (01).jpg|thumb|right|The purpose-built Burton store in [[East Ham]], east London]] Burton has worked with the Bobby Moore Fund in order to publicize the issue of bowel cancer.{{cite news|last1=Hardie|first1=Charlotte|title=Charity begins on the high street|url=https://www.retail-week.com/charity-begins-on-the-high-street/1845401.article|work=Retail Week|date=11 September 2008|language=en}} England's World-Cup-winning football team captain [[Bobby Moore]] died of bowel cancer in 1993. The Bobby Moore Fund is an arm of [[Cancer Research UK]]. In November 2009, Burton sought to bring back "The Burton", a style of [[moustache]] worn by founder Montague Burton, through their support of the [[Movember]] campaign in order to raise money for The Prostate Cancer Charity.{{Citation needed|date=May 2017}} The "Burton" moustache was styled upon two influential moustache types, the English and the Handlebar. ==Notes== {{notelist}} ==References== {{reflist|30em}} ==External links== {{commons category|Burtons (retailer)}} * {{official website|http://www.burton.co.uk}} * {{PM20|FID=co/001452|TEXT=Documents and clippings about|NAME=}} {{Arcadia Group}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:1903 establishments in England]] [[Category:2021 disestablishments in England]] [[Category:2021 disestablishments in the United Kingdom]] [[Category:2021 mergers and acquisitions]] [[Category:British companies established in 1903]] [[Category:Clothing companies of England]] [[Category:Clothing companies based in London]] [[Category:Clothing companies established in 1903]] [[Category:Clothing retailers of England]] [[Category:Companies based in the City of Westminster]] [[Category:Companies formerly listed on the London Stock Exchange]] [[Category:Retail companies disestablished in 2021]] [[Category:Retail companies established in 1903]] [[Category:Companies that have entered administration in the United Kingdom]] [[Category:Companies that have filed for Chapter 15 bankruptcy]]

Burton Online Limited (trading as Burton Menswear) is a British online clothing retailer, former high street retailer and clothing manufacturer, specialising in men's clothing and footwear. It is operated by Debenhams Group in the United Kingdom.
Previously, Burton was a constituent of the FTSE 100 Index, but became a trading name of Arcadia Group Brands Ltd, part of the Arcadia Group. Sir Philip Green acquired the Arcadia Group in 2002, and it became the sole owner of Burton. In 2021, Boohoo Group (now Debenhams Group) acquired the brand after Arcadia went into administration.
